newsitem.title: UK: Sterling steadies but traders wary of correction.
newsitem.headline: Sterling steadies but traders wary of correction.

text.p: Sterling steadied after its near-three-pfennig tumble against the mark on Thursday, but traders are not yet convinced that its correction is over.
The pound fell victim to profit taking after it surged more than eight pfennigs in two trading days to set a six-and-a-half-year high of 3.0327 marks on Monday.
It has since stabilised and traders are now looking for it to take its cue from U.S. data and any comments by European policy makers on European economic and monetary union.
Independent sterling strength is not on the cards anytime soon, though, they said.
"Traders have been looking to lighten their long positions on any move up," said a trader on the Dublin floor of FINEX, the financial products division of the New York Cotton Exchange.
"They are still long but we will have to break convincingly above 3.0 before they start building these positions up again."
Sterling/mark was at 3.0020/30 at 1020 GMT against 3.0010/20 late Thursday in Europe. Cable was at $1.6726/36 against $1.6735/46 yesterday.
The pound's trade-weighted index was at 104.9, up from 104.7 at Thursday's close but below the near-seven-year high of 105.7 it hit on Monday.

UK data briefly boosted the pound as high as 3.0070 marks and to $1.6767 in the morning European session. M4 grew at an annual rate of 11.6 percent in June, the fastest seasonally adjusted rate of growth since December 1990.
Also, the British Bankers Association reported a 3.934 billion sterling increase in total sterling lending to the private sector, with mortgage lending rising by 905 million pounds in the month.
While sterling quickly pared its gains, the data reinforced expectations that domestic demand is strong enough to warrant higher UK interest rates.
The widening premium UK rates are expected to offer over German and other continental rates should keep the pound underpinned in the coming weeks analyst said.
"A lot is priced on UK interest rates and growth but the economy should remain firm and sterling will continue to benefit," said Brian Martin, currency strategist at BZW.
He predicted sterling would climb to 3.10 marks in the coming months before a deterioration in the UK's trade and current account position dented bullishness about its prospects.
Meantime, trading in cable is expected to take its cue from the dollar's reaction to U.S. trade data later today.
Comments by German policy makers about the mark's weakness against the dollar or European economic and monetary union will determine sterling/mark's fate, traders said.
"The dollar could be the focus of attention later today but at the moment it seems to be a mark story," said the trader at FINEX.
